findings.reason: a node can satisfy its gate with a retry that writes every pending plan and still tells the caller the move is partial, so the section would land the same class of misreport one layer up unless the plan fixes the induction to fail across the first retry and states what a retry that clears the pending set returns.
findings.text: the done-when's first case and its stated failure induction contradict each other: the case needs a first retry that reports the partial write instead of success, but "making the plan's own write raise once the index has been written" means that retry finds the plan writable, so §9's own mechanism ("for each pending plan that is now writable it applies only that plan's sprint write … once none is pending the receipt records success") either clears the pending entry in that same call — returning `ok: false, error: partial_write` for a move that is now fully written, the misreport §9 exists to remove — or the case cannot be produced at all; the two readings differ in what the retry returns and nothing in the section selects between them
